overview: Rise 6.1.30's Scaffold (727 lines) is the client's full bridging pipeline. The PreUpdate handler runs the expand extrapolation, same-Y gating, the Slot component's delayed silent slot switch, the ticksOnAir accounting and the canPlace gate (which consults BadPacketsComponent), then PlayerUtil.getPlacePossibility and getEnumFacing resolve the target cell and click face, calculateRotations drives six placement modes (Normal, Godbridge, Breesily, Snap, Telly, Eagle), and place() either calls rightClickMouse under the default Strict rayCast or onPlayerRightClick followed by a queued C0APacketAnimation. Rotations flow through RotationComponent.setRotations into the movement packet while the local rotationYaw/rotationPitch stay untouched, the Slot component switches the hotbar silently with a C09 sent outside the event bus, and the eleven tower modes range from the NCP floor-snap (posY % 1 <= 0.00153598) through onGround-spoofed re-applies to fake item-only C08s. A timer setting (0.1-10) and ten sprint modes, several of which emit C0B action packets, round out the module.

sections.p: The PreUpdate handler iterates recursion passes, sets mc.thePlayer.safeWalk from the safeWalk setting, resets right/left binds, and runs the expand scan: when expand is nonzero it walks blocks ahead along MoveUtil.direction and shifts the placement offset to the first air cell. sameY pins placements to startY (the floor of posY at enable) when the sameY mode is not Off or the Speed module is enabled, and the Slot component's setSlotDelayed switches the hotbar with a 25% random skip. ticksOnAir increments while the block one below is replaceable, and canPlace requires the BadPacketsComponent gate to pass and ticksOnAir to exceed the random placeDelay draw (default 0-0). getPlacePossibility resolves the target cell, getEnumFacing derives the click face, and place() runs only when RayCastUtil.overBlock passes for the resolved face and cell, or rayCast is Off. A PacketReceiveEvent listener runs PacketUtil.correctBlockCount to repair ghost-item stacks the server reports, and the timer setting scales mc.timer.timerSpeed while enabled.

calculateRotations switches on the mode value. Normal refreshes the aim only when the mouse-over disagrees with the cached face; Godbridge snaps yaw to cardinal minus 180 at pitch 76.4, swaps the movement keys, holds sneak while directionalChange is under 10 and re-randomizes drift when the server yaw gap exceeds 10; Breesily holds pitch 80 with drift and presses strafe keys to steer back onto the block line; Snap ray-scans then pins yaw to the movement direction; Telly right-click-mouses at offGroundTicks 0 and 2 and aims inside the 3-7 window; Eagle snaps to 45-degree yaw steps at pitch 78, right-click-mouses under a 0.5 (ground) or 0.2 (air) random gate and emulates sneak. RotationComponent.setRotations smooths toward the target with rotationSpeed * 36, applies the MovementFix strafe rewrite when movement correction is on, and the local rotationYaw assignment is commented out, so the aim reaches the server through the movement packet only. getRotations ray-casts from a temporarily lowered eye position in 45-degree yaw steps to find a look that RayCastUtil.overBlock accepts, then falls back to a direct face calculation.

The sprint modes manage the C0B surface: Normal leaves vanilla sprint alone, Disabled clears it, and the Bypass, Vulcan, Verus, Matrix and Watchdog variants toggle sneak or sprint state, with VulcanSprint emitting C0BPacketEntityAction START/STOP_SNEAKING pairs and MatrixSprint pressing the sneak key every 4 ticks. The tower modes write motionY from PreMotion, Strafe or PacketSend listeners: NCPTower queues a fake C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement(null) on every tick and applies the classic floor-snap, setting motionY 0.42 only when posY % 1 <= 0.00153598 and snapping position to the floor; VanillaTower and NormalTower jump from ground only (NormalTower also clamps motionY to -0.0784 when the placement C08 for the cell two below goes out); AirJumpTower re-applies 0.42 every second tick with an onGround(true) spoof; MatrixTower re-applies 0.42 whenever motionY drops under 0.2 with the same spoof; VulcanTower re-applies 0.42 after offGroundTicks exceeds 3 with more fake C08s; MMCTower kills sprint when the placement C08 fires and sets 0.42; LegitTower calls the vanilla jump; TestTower (Verus) uses 0.81/0.78 impulses.

files.label: Scaffold.java
files.explanation: The complete module: settings, the PreUpdate pipeline (expand, sameY, slot delay, ticksOnAir, canPlace, target resolution, calculateRotations, place), the six placement modes, the eagle and sneak timing (calculateSneaking), getHitVec with the ray-cast-corrected hit vector, place() with the Strict/Off rayCast split, getRotations with the lowered-eye scan, and the mode values for sprint, tower and downwards whose classes live in the scaffold subpackages.

files.label: PlayerUtil.java (block search and facing)
files.explanation: The world-facing utility the PreUpdate handler depends on: getPlacePossibility scans candidate air cells for the placement target, getEnumFacing probes the neighbor cells and returns an EnumFacingOffset wrapping the click face and its offset, blockRelativeToPlayer and blockAheadOfPlayer drive the expand scan, the ticksOnAir test and the isBlockUnder checks used by the tower modes, and blockNear feeds the tower gating. Every placement the module makes is derived from these methods, so the file defines what the C08 stream looks like.

countering.label: NCP blockplace Scaffold check (angle / time / sprint / rotate / tool-switch)
countering.explanation: The dedicated detector gates on a bridging profile (horizontal face, block 1-2 below the previous y, solid, within 2.0 blocks) and runs five sub-checks. Angle flags look-versus-face-normal beyond MAX_ANGLE 90 degrees: the Normal and Snap modes aim ray-verified at the face and pass, while the fixed profiles do not, Godbridge at pitch 76.4 and Breesily at pitch 80 against UP faces put the look more than 90 degrees off the face normal on every placement, and the Snap profile's pitch 90 does the same. Time records placement ticks at pitch over 70 with no sneak and no speed potion, and flags an average interval below scaffoldTimeAvg: the default placeDelay 0-0 places every tick, so the average is near 1 and the violation fires, with the sneak submodes as the only relief and they are off by default. Sprint flags a placement within 8 ticks of sprinting at yDistance under 0.1 and jumpPhase under 4, which the sprint modes that place while sprinting satisfy. ToolSwitch flags any held-slot change between placements and sets cancelNextPlace, and the Slot component's silent C09 switch is exactly a held-slot change, so a mixed hotbar trips it and starves the placement stream through the same BlockPlaceListener pass.

countering.label: NCP blockplace FastPlace (placement rate window)
countering.explanation: FastPlace accumulates accepted placements into an ActionFrequency(2, 1000) two-second window plus a short-term same-tick counter and flags when the window score exceeds cc.fastPlaceLimit. The default configuration places once per client tick, about 20 per second, which holds the window several times over the limit for the whole bridge. The module's dials map directly onto the check: the placeDelay random bounds (0-5 ticks) spread placements when raised and lower the score; the timer setting (0.1-10) multiplies the client tick rate, so each server second can carry more than 20 C08s and the window rises with the multiplier; and the tower path places at most once per jump cycle, which stays under the window. Hawk's BlockInteractSpeed is the same-tick binary complement: the fake item-only C08s (position -1, face 255) that the NCP and Vulcan towers queue never produce a Bukkit BlockPlaceEvent, so FastPlace never sees them, but Hawk counts every PacketPlayInBlockPlace, and a fake plus a real placement in the same server tick trips its same-tick test.

countering.label: NCP blockplace Direction (look ray vs clicked face)
countering.explanation: Direction ray-traces from the eye with the server-side yaw/pitch of the last C03 against the claimed clicked block, sampling the look at the right point of the movement queue, and accumulates the angular deviation into directionVL with 0.9 per-tick decay. With the default Strict rayCast, place() goes through rightClickMouse, so the C08 is a genuine click whose look the RotationComponent wrote into the same tick's movement packet, and the server ray crosses the face, keeping the check quiet on straight bridges. The failure modes are the ones where the C03 look and the C08 face diverge: Snap's random-yaw ticks, Telly's aim only inside the offGroundTicks 3-7 window, the rotationSpeed * 36 smoothing lag during fast turns, and the rayCast Off path, which places through onPlayerRightClick without the overBlock gate. At one placement per tick the accumulated violations outrun the decay when any of those modes is active.

countering.label: NCP SurvivalFly (jump envelope vs tower modes)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's jump envelope credits exactly one impulse per MAX_JUMP_DELAY = 10 ticks and only when the yDistance matches the predicted jump gain with a from-ground state read from the block cache. That splits the tower modes in two. NCPTower passes: the floor-snap at posY % 1 <= 0.00153598 returns the player to the ground, motionY 0.42 is applied only at the snap, and every impulse is a fresh ground jump within the prediction epsilon. VanillaTower, NormalTower and LegitTower pass for the same reason: they jump from ground only. AirJumpTower (re-apply every second tick), MatrixTower (re-apply whenever motionY drops under 0.2, with an onGround(true) spoof that NCP ignores because ground state comes from the block cache), VulcanTower (re-apply after offGroundTicks > 3) and TestTower (0.81/0.78 impulses) all re-apply jump-scale motion inside the jumpDelay window, so the move is not credited, the allowed distance stays at the momentum prediction, and a yDistance near 0.4 yields a violation of 30+ with a set-back. The fake C08(null) towers are invisible to this check but feed Hawk's placement counter as described under FastPlace.
